articles.title: Shocking allegations against Rashod Bateman: Arrested after allegedly smashing the windows of a car with a 3-month-old baby inside
articles.standfirst: Baltimore Ravens wide receiver faces multiple charges stemming from a June incident in Georgia as his attorney insists the situation has been “taken completely out of context”
articles.summary: Baltimore Ravens wide receiver faces multiple charges stemming from a June incident in Georgia as his attorney insists the situation has been “taken completely out of context”
articles.body:
B altimore Ravens wide receiver Rashod Bateman is facing multiple charges following an alleged family violence incident in Georgia that involved the mother of his child and their three-month-old baby.

According to court documents and an arrest warrant obtained by TMZ, the incident allegedly occurred at around 6 a.m. on June 3 in Walton County.

Authorities allege that Bateman used an object to damage the windshield and driver's-side window of a 2021 Mercedes-Benz while the woman and the infant were inside the vehicle.

The documents state that shattered glass caused multiple small cuts to the alleged victim's face. Police reportedly observed glass fragments on her face when they spoke with her and also documented multiple contusions.

The couple's three-month-old child was reportedly seated in a car seat in the back row of the vehicle when the alleged incident took place, adding another disturbing element to the case.

Bateman , who is 26, surrendered to the Walton County Sheriff's Office on the same day, according to his representatives and multiple reports.

The charges reported by NFL .com include misdemeanor battery involving family violence, reckless conduct and first-degree criminal damage to property. The case remains pending, meaning the allegations have not been established as facts in court.

Bateman's attorney disputes the portrayal of the incident

The wide receiver's legal team has pushed back against the way the allegations have been characterized publicly.

Jordan Siev , an attorney for Bateman at Reed Smith , told TMZ: "It is unfortunate that a personal family situation has been taken completely out of context for sensational reasons. We will let the court process play out and the facts will come out at that time."

Bateman's legal position will now be tested through the court process, with the available records providing the allegations from the authorities rather than a final determination of what happened.

There have also been developments involving the restrictions placed on Bateman following his arrest. A no-contact order was initially imposed, but Bateman later asked the court to remove it, arguing that the alleged victim wanted to resume contact with him.

The court ultimately approved the request, although restrictions remained in place. Bateman was ordered not to have violent contact with the woman, while his ability to see her was tied to completing a class, according to reports.

The Baltimore Ravens have also acknowledged the situation and said they have been communicating with their player.

"We are aware of the situation involving Rashod and have been in direct communication with him. We notified the league office and have been cooperating throughout the process. As this is a pending legal matter, we will not have further comment."

The NFL has been notified and is reviewing the case, according to NFL.com.

The allegations arrive at a particularly significant point in Bateman's career. The former first-round pick has spent his entire NFL career with Baltimore after being selected No. 27 overall in the 2021 draft.

He enjoyed his strongest campaign in 2024, producing 756 receiving yards and nine touchdowns, which helped earn him a three-year contract extension worth $36.75 million with $20 million guaranteed.

The deal keeps him under contract through the 2029 season.

His production subsequently fell sharply in 2025, when he finished with 224 yards and two touchdowns on 19 receptions. Nevertheless, Baltimore continues to view him as an important component of its receiving group.

Bateman has been involved with the Ravens during preparations for the 2026 season, making the legal developments particularly relevant to the franchise as it considers how the NFL's review could affect his availability.

For now, however, the central issue remains the legal case in Georgia. Authorities are still dealing with allegations arising from the June incident, while Bateman's attorney has urged people to wait for the facts to emerge through the court process.

Neither the accusations nor the surrounding circumstances amount to a conviction, and the case remains ongoing as Bateman prepares for the next stage of his NFL career.

articles.title: Lamar Jackson does not hide his fears ahead of the game against the Dallas Cowboys
articles.standfirst: Lamar Jackson ignores Maracanã concerns and focuses on beating the Cowboys in Brazil.
articles.summary: Lamar Jackson ignores Maracanã concerns and focuses on beating the Cowboys in Brazil.
articles.body:
Lamar Jackson made his stance crystal clear on one of the biggest talking points ahead of the historic Week 3 showdown between the Baltimore Ravens and the Dallas Cowboys in Rio de Janeiro : the condition of the playing surface at Maracanã Stadium.

The Ravens quarterback was asked Wednesday about concerns surrounding the field, but insisted it's not something that deserves his attention.

I think the NFL do a great job of having their specialists go out there and, you know, look over the field. I can't worry about that. I just gotta worry about getting us a dub in Brazil, our first time in Rio. I feel we done played on bad fields plenty of times, so I can't really dwell on that. We're just going there to play football.

The comments reflect the mindset Baltimore is taking into its trip to Brazil , just days after suffering a surprising 24-17 loss to the New Orleans Saints in Week 2. That defeat prompted Jackson to call for an immediate response after the Ravens once again squandered a fourth-quarter lead.

Now, Baltimore will try to bounce back against the Cowboys , a challenge made even tougher with its top wide receiver still sidelined from practice. Even so, Jackson insists the team's performance—not the playing surface—remains the only priority.

Lamar Jackson refuses to let field concerns become a distraction

Jackson knows the Ravens have much bigger issues to address than the condition of the Maracanã pitch.

Against the Saints , Baltimore's offense struggled to find rhythm as Jackson failed to establish chemistry with the receiver filling in for injured Zay Flowers . The offensive line also had a difficult afternoon, allowing New Orleans' pass rush to generate constant pressure and record three sacks.

Offensive coordinator Declan Doyle also came under fire after virtually abandoning Derrick Henry in the second half, a decision that drew criticism from several former NFL players.

Baltimore is still searching for the explosive offensive identity many expected entering the season, but the team's concerns extend well beyond that side of the ball.

Maracanã field conditions remain under scrutiny

While Jackson and teammate Kyle Hamilton have downplayed the controversy, NFL field director Nick Pappas attempted to calm concerns by saying there are "no concerns at this time" regarding the playing surface.

However, that assessment differs from comments made by players from Brazilian club Flamengo , which calls the Maracanã home. Midfielder Giorgian De Arrascaeta recently claimed that "the field keeps getting worse."

Inside the Ravens' locker room, the message is simple: stay focused on football. Even so, head coach Jesse Minter and general manager Eric DeCosta will undoubtedly keep a close eye on the field conditions. The concern is understandable, especially after the Washington Commanders and New York Giants both lost their starting quarterbacks to serious injuries during the opening weeks of the season.

articles.title: Tyler Loop “mocks” the Cowboys and recreates Cristiano Ronaldo's celebration at the Maracana: “Siuuuuuu”
articles.standfirst: Loop scored a last-gasp field goal to defeat the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday
articles.summary: Loop scored a last-gasp field goal to defeat the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday
articles.body:
Tyler Loop delivered the winning moment for the Baltimore Ravens in Brazil, then borrowed one of soccer's most recognizable celebrations as the Maracana erupted with a familiar “ siuuuu ”.

The Ravens kicker drilled a 56-yard field goal with one second remaining to beat the Dallas Cowboys 34-31, but Loop 's celebration afterward provided an equally memorable ending to an extraordinary night in Rio de Janeiro .

After watching his kick sail through the uprights, Loop broke into Cristiano Ronaldo 's trademark celebration, performing the famous leap and landing pose as more than 72,000 fans inside the Maracana responded with the familiar “ Siuuuu ” associated with the Portuguese soccer superstar.

The celebration capped a remarkable final sequence. Dallas had tied the game at 31-31 through Brandon Aubrey 's 23-yard field goal with seven seconds remaining, seemingly sending the contest toward overtime.

Lamar Jackson then found Zay Flowers for a 27-yard completion before alertly calling timeout with one second left. That gave Loop the opportunity to attempt the decisive kick, and the rookie delivered from 56 yards to complete the Ravens ' dramatic victory.

Loop 's celebration came after one of the most dramatic finishes of the NFL season. The Ravens improved to 2-1 after repeatedly answering Dallas ' attempts to take control.

Derrick Henry rushed for 89 yards and two touchdowns, while Jackson helped Baltimore recover from a difficult opening stretch. The Ravens led 24-13 in the third quarter before Dallas responded with a series of big plays.

Dak Prescott connected with Jake Ferguson for a 19-yard touchdown before KaVontae Turpin 's 9-yard touchdown run put Dallas ahead 28-24 with less than 10 minutes remaining.

Jackson then led Baltimore down the field, eventually finding rookie tight end Matt Hibner for a 2-yard touchdown that restored the Ravens ' lead at 31-28 with 1:30 left. Dallas answered with Aubrey 's tying kick, but Jackson and Flowers gave the team just enough time to set up Loop.

The Ravens will look for their third victory of the season against the Tennessee Titans on Sunday, October 4 with Jackson facing off against the overall first pick in the 2025 NFL Draft , Cam Ward .

How Cristiano Ronaldo's “Siuuuu” became a global celebration

Ronaldo 's celebration first emerged in 2013, when he was playing for Real Madrid against Chelsea in the International Champions Cup. After scoring with a header, he sprinted toward the corner before jumping, turning in the air and landing with his legs spread and arms extended.

Ronaldo has explained that the celebration developed naturally as whist at Real Madrid , he had been using the Spanish word “ si ,” meaning “ yes ,” and the extended “ siuuuu ” eventually became associated with his goals.

The celebration subsequently became a ritual involving both Ronaldo and the supporters. His leap, mid-air rotation and wide-legged landing became instantly recognizable, while crowds began responding with the elongated “ siuuuu !” after he landed.

Its reach eventually extended well beyond soccer after Ronaldo famously performed the celebration after winning the 2014 Ballon d'Or. Numerous athletes have since adopted their own versions, including Jeremiah Smith , Manel Kape , Nick Kyrgios , Carlos Alcaraz , Rory McIlroy and now Loop .

YouTuber IShowSpeed has also become closely associated with the celebration. A prominent Ronaldo fan, Speed regularly recreates the jump, spin and landing for his enormous online audience, helping take the gesture even further beyond the soccer world.

articles.title: Diego Pavia announces surprising football comeback and he won't be alone: Several teammates also returning
articles.standfirst: The former Heisman finalist has identified a possible route back into professional football and hopes to bring familiar faces with him
articles.summary: The former Heisman finalist has identified a possible route back into professional football and hopes to bring familiar faces with him
articles.body:
A year after establishing himself as one of college football's most recognizable quarterbacks, Diego Pavia is preparing for another opportunity to prove he belongs in the professional game.

The former Vanderbilt star experienced a disappointing introduction to the NFL after going unselected in the 2026 draft and subsequently being released by the Baltimore Ravens before training camp.

Without another NFL offer, Pavia appeared to be moving toward a career in streaming, raising questions about whether his playing days had already ended.

However, the quarterback has now outlined a different plan, revealing his interest in joining the United Football League in 2027.

His ambitions extend beyond securing a roster spot for himself, with Pavia also hoping to reunite with several former teammates.

During a recent YouTube appearance, Pavia discussed his future and indicated that he was exploring an opportunity in the UFL.

"I plan on doing some UFL if everything goes smooth," Pavia said.

He also suggested that he wanted to bring former teammates into the league, although he did not publicly identify the players involved.

The comments mark a change in direction after his unsuccessful attempt to establish himself in the NFL.

Pavia 's professional prospects initially appeared promising following a college career that culminated in national recognition and a place among the Heisman Trophy finalists.

Nevertheless, the transition proved difficult, with Baltimore deciding not to retain him ahead of training camp.

A UFL opportunity would allow Pavia to return to competitive football while potentially putting himself back on the radar of NFL teams.

Why Diego Pavia's NFL opportunity ended so quickly

Pavia developed a reputation at Vanderbilt as a competitive dual-threat quarterback capable of extending plays and producing moments of individual brilliance.

His performances earned widespread attention during his final college season, although questions remained about how his playing style would translate to the NFL.

Those concerns contributed to a difficult draft experience, with all 32 franchises passing on the quarterback.

Baltimore subsequently offered him an opportunity, but his time with the organization ended before he could compete for a place during training camp.

Although the setback left Pavia without an NFL team, playing in a spring football league could provide the game experience necessary to strengthen his professional credentials.

When is the 2027 UFL Draft?

The UFL has scheduled its 2027 draft for November 18, 2026, in St. Louis, Missouri.

The event will consist of 15 rounds, with the opening two rounds broadcast on NFL Network, giving prospective players another opportunity to enter professional football.

Pavia hasn't announced an agreement with a specific UFL franchise, and his participation remains dependent on how his plans develop.

His suggestion that former teammates could join him also remains a possibility rather than a confirmed arrangement.

Nevertheless, the quarterback's comments indicate that his ambitions have not disappeared following his brief NFL experience.

A successful spell in the UFL wouldn't guarantee another opportunity in the NFL, but it could provide the platform Pavia needs to demonstrate that his football career still has another chapter.

articles.title: Eli Manning’s honest admission about Ed Reed will instantly grab Ravens fans' attention
articles.standfirst: Ed Reed's incredible instincts left even a two-time Super Bowl MVP second-guessing himself
articles.summary: Ed Reed's incredible instincts left even a two-time Super Bowl MVP second-guessing himself
articles.body:
Eli Manning spent 16 seasons facing some of the NFL's most dangerous defensive players, but Baltimore Ravens legend Ed Reed clearly left a lasting impression.

The former New York Giants quarterback recently opened up about the difficulties of preparing to face the Hall of Fame safety, revealing that Reed was even more dangerous than his game footage suggested.

Speaking on The Colin Cowherd Podcast, Manning explained how watching Reed on film sometimes created the impression that the safety was making mistakes.

However, Manning quickly discovered that Reed was operating on a different level.

“You kind of saw it on film that he was smooth, {but} you're kind of watching it and you're like, ‘well, I don't think Ed's doing the right thing here. Maybe that was a bust and we can take advantage of it,'” Manning said.

“Then you realize he's just smarter. He just knew how to read eyes, and he was just such a natural, attracted to the ball. He was like the scariest person.

Manning admitted that he eventually became reluctant to throw anywhere near the former Ravens star.

The Giants quarterback's encounter with Reed in December 2004 remains particularly memorable. Facing Baltimore, Manning completed just four of 18 passes for 27 yards and threw two interceptions. Reed secured one of those turnovers as the Ravens delivered a convincing 37-14 victory.

Manning was eventually benched in the second half, making the afternoon even more difficult for the young quarterback.

Reed , meanwhile, was enjoying one of the finest seasons of his career.

The former Miami Hurricanes standout finished 2004 with nine interceptions for 358 return yards, earning NFL Defensive Player of the Year honors. It was also the first of five First-Team All-Pro selections during his remarkable career.

Ed Reed's criticism adds another layer to Ravens frustration

Manning's comments are particularly interesting given the recent frustrations surrounding Reed's former team.

Following Baltimore's disappointing 35-13 defeat against the Cincinnati Bengals on October 25, the Ravens legend publicly questioned the coaching decisions being made by the organization.

Reed posted a blunt reaction on social media, writing: "Wow, terrible coaching decisions week in week out crazy!"

Baltimore had entered halftime with a 13-0 advantage but completely lost control after the break. Cincinnati scored five second-half touchdowns, while quarterback Joe Burrow threw four touchdown passes to complete the comeback.

The Ravens struggled to respond offensively, too. Zay Flowers had enjoyed an impressive first half, but Baltimore couldn't maintain that production. Backup quarterback Tyler Huntley also struggled to find consistent solutions against Cincinnati's adjustments.

Running back Derrick Henry's difficulties in short-yardage situations added to the frustration, with questionable offensive decisions becoming another talking point.

Although Reed didn't identify specific plays or coaches in his criticism, his reaction showed the growing concerns surrounding Baltimore's inability to protect halftime advantages.

Manning's admission offers another reminder to Ravens fans of just how special Reed was. His ability to anticipate plays, recognize opportunities and punish quarterbacks made him an extraordinary defensive presence.

articles.title: From Russell Wilson to Jimmy Garoppolo: Ranking the Ravens' potential quarterback options
articles.standfirst: The franchise could need an experienced leader capable of joining it quickly
articles.summary: The franchise could need an experienced leader capable of joining it quickly
articles.body:
The Baltimore Ravens entered Sunday's game against the Buffalo Bills expecting Lamar Jackson to lead the offense in a critical AFC matchup. Instead, they found themselves confronting a quarterback emergency that could force the front office to look outside the organization for help.

Jackson was ruled out after injuring his right thumb on Baltimore's first offensive snap. The two-time NFL MVP had just returned after missing three games because of an ankle injury, making the setback especially frustrating for a Ravens team trying to regain momentum.

Then the situation became more complicated. Backup Tyler Huntley suffered a toe injury in the first half and was questionable to return, leaving undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano to take over under center. Huntley completed just two of four passes for zero yards before exiting. Suddenly, the Ravens' quarterback depth chart looked like a potential roster emergency rather than a routine injury contingency.

If Jackson's thumb injury forces him to miss additional time and Huntley's toe keeps him from being available, Baltimore could need an experienced quarterback capable of joining the team quickly. Several recognizable names are worth considering, including Russell Wilson, Jimmy Garoppolo, Andy Dalton, Jake Browning, Kyle Trask and Bailey Zappe. But which one makes the most sense for a team that still has ambitions of competing in the AFC?

Jimmy Garoppolo: The most practical short-term option

Garoppolo stands out as a logical candidate if Baltimore wants an experienced quarterback who can provide stability while Jackson recovers. He has played in multiple offensive systems, has extensive regular-season experience and has appeared in two Super Bowls with the San Francisco 49ers.

Garoppolo is not a replacement for Jackson's unique running ability or improvisational playmaking. His value would instead come from operating a conventional passing game, getting the ball out quickly and avoiding the mistakes that can turn a difficult injury situation into a season-defining crisis.

The Ravens could lean more heavily on Derrick Henry and their running game, use play-action to create opportunities downfield and ask Garoppolo to make timely decisions rather than carry the offense by himself. That approach would not reproduce everything Baltimore does with Jackson . It could, however, provide a workable temporary plan.

Garoppolo was listed as an unrestricted free agent in 2026, making him one of the more straightforward names to investigate. His health and current readiness would still need to be evaluated before a deal.

Russell Wilson: The biggest name available

Wilson offers one of the strongest résumés among the potential candidates. The former Seattle Seahawks star won a Super Bowl, has played in numerous postseason games and has experience handling the expectations that come with quarterbacking a high-profile franchise.

His ability to move outside the pocket and create opportunities when protection breaks down could also help Baltimore maintain some flexibility if Jackson is unavailable. There are caveats. Wilson is 37, and his recent career has been less consistent than his peak years in Seattle.

His playing style also differs from Jackson's , meaning the Ravens would need to adjust their offense rather than expect the veteran to duplicate the injured starter's production. Still, if Baltimore wants a quarterback who has handled big games and could be asked to start immediately, Wilson deserves serious consideration. He was also listed as an unrestricted free agent in 2026.

Andy Dalton: The experienced insurance policy

Dalton brings one of the longest résumés on this list. The former Bengals quarterback has made 169 regular-season starts and has spent time in several offensive systems during his NFL career. His familiarity with the AFC North is another potential advantage. Dalton spent the first nine seasons of his career in Cincinnati, facing the Ravens and their divisional rivals twice each year.

The challenge is availability. Dalton signed with the Atlanta Falcons in October after being released by the Philadelphia Eagles, so Baltimore would need to acquire him from Atlanta rather than simply sign him off the free-agent market.

His age and limited recent playing time would also be considerations. Nevertheless, Dalton's experience makes him a name worth monitoring if the Ravens decide to explore a trade.

Jake Browning: Familiarity with the AFC North

Browning would be an intriguing option because he has already demonstrated that he can handle an extended opportunity as an NFL starter. With Cincinnati in 2023, he stepped in for Joe Burrow and helped the Bengals remain competitive, showing that he could operate an offense under pressure.

He would also bring familiarity with the Ravens' division and the defensive challenges Baltimore faces throughout the season. However, Browning signed with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers for 2026, according to the league's free-agent tracking information.

That means he is not simply available for Baltimore to sign; the Ravens would have to explore a trade or wait for a change in his status. His experience is attractive, but the contractual situation makes him a less immediate option than an available free agent.

Kyle Trask: A developmental alternative

Trask offers a different profile from the veteran candidates. The former Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback has spent much of his professional career developing behind established starters rather than accumulating extensive regular-season experience.

He could appeal to a team looking for a younger arm who might benefit from a change of scenery. But Baltimore's immediate circumstances make this a difficult time to prioritize development.

Trask was under contract with Tampa Bay in 2026, meaning the Ravens would need to determine whether he was obtainable. Unless the team sees significant upside in his ability to learn the offense quickly, he would be a riskier short-term choice than an experienced starter.

Jackson was ruled out after injuring his right thumb on Baltimore's first offensive snap. The two-time NFL MVP had just returned after missing three games because of an ankle injury, making the setback especially frustrating for a Ravens team trying to regain momentum.

Then the situation became more complicated. Backup Tyler Huntley suffered a toe injury in the first half and was questionable to return, leaving undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano to take over under center. Huntley completed just two of four passes for zero yards before exiting. Suddenly, the Ravens' quarterback depth chart looked like a potential roster emergency rather than a routine injury contingency.

If Jackson's thumb injury forces him to miss additional time and Huntley's toe keeps him from being available, Baltimore could need an experienced quarterback capable of joining the team quickly.
